haiku-low.q1: 10 minutes. An unclaimed hold is marked EXPIRED by a per-minute Inventory timer and its stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, the order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, short items are listed, no payment is requested, and the cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q3: Charges use the order id as idempotency key, retries reuse it, and Payment allows one payment row per order id.
haiku-low.q4: Payment refunds the full amount. Order marks CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, publishes RefundRequested, and emails the customer that the order is cancelled and refund is coming. The cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q5: Only on OrderConfirmed, by cart id and version. On short stock, decline or out-of-stock cancellation, the cart is left exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service drives the steps. Its record is the order, with status history and frozen lines and prices.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which checks its signature and then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker for Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks the provider event id against its inbox and replies 200 OK without acting on repeats. The event id is saved with the status change in one transaction.
haiku-low.q9: Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderFailed. That event triggers Inventory to release the hold at once, or do nothing if it already expired.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory decides in one transaction. Active hold: claim. Lapsed but unsold: retake it and fulfil (a design choice). Sold to someone else: StockClaimFailed, leading to refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is marked REFUND_FAILED with the error recorded, and a backoff retry timer re-runs it. After max retries it becomes REFUND_STUCK and finance is alerted. It is tracked in Payment.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published after StockClaimed. The Cart service empties the cart on that event.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes unless the order claims it. If unclaimed after 10 minutes, a timer (every minute) marks the reservation EXPIRED and puts the stock back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before payment. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, replies SHORT with the short items, Order marks REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK and tells the customer which items are short; no payment is requested and the cart is untouched.
sonnet.q3: Payment retries with the same idempotency key (the order id), and there is only one payment row per order id, so the provider treats it as the same request.
sonnet.q4: Payment refunds in full (REFUND_PENDING row, then provider refund with key refund-<order id>); Order marks the order CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer that it is cancelled and a full refund is coming. Nothing ships; cart untouched.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed (by cart id and version). On failure (short stock, declined payment, out-of-stock cancellation) the cart is left exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: Events on the shared message broker (plus some HTTP calls) move it between services. The record of progress is the order status in the Order service's database (status history), keyed by order id.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook (HTTP) to Payment, which saves the status and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event on the broker; Order consumes it.
sonnet.q8: Payment checks the provider's event id in its inbox; if already seen it replies 200 OK and does nothing. New ones save the event id and status in one transaction. Consumers of broker events also use an inbox of handled event ids.
sonnet.q9: Inventory releases the hold at once (does nothing if already released or expired). Trigger: Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes the OrderFailed event, which Inventory consumes.
sonnet.q10: On ClaimStock Inventory decides in one transaction: if the hold is still active, claim it; if lapsed but the stock is still unsold, it takes the stock again for this order (fulfil, no refund; a stated design choice); if lapsed and the stock was sold to someone else, it publishes StockClaimFailed, leading to cancellation and full refund.
sonnet.q11: Refund becomes REFUND_FAILED with the error recorded, and a retry timer re-runs it with backoff. After max retries it becomes REFUND_STUCK, an alert goes to finance, and the row stays open with retries continuing. It is tracked in Payment's refunds data (status, attempt count, last error).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (published by Order) triggers the Cart service to empty the cart, by cart id and version so lines added after Place order are kept.
